correctness.rationale: A tree has no cyclic orientations. Conditional on the hub edge pointing out, both arm orientations contribute z; conditional on it pointing in, the arm contributes 1+z, excluding the hub. Thus the initial product is (1+3z)^m, with hub-sink correction (z−1)(1+z)^m. The binomial coefficients give degree m+1, a simple zero at 0 and no positive zero. At z=−y with 0<y≤1/3 the quotient (1−3y)/(1−y) is in [0,1) and cannot have mth power 1+y; y=1 is not a root either. For 1/3<y<1 and even m, the ratio [(3y−1)/(1−y)]^m/(1+y) increases from zero to infinity with strictly positive logarithmic derivative 2m/[(3y−1)(1−y)]−1/(1+y). It is 2/3 at 1/2, giving one simple root with magnitude above 1/2; odd m gives opposite signs on that interval. For y>1 the ratio [3+2/(y−1)]^m/(1+y) has strictly negative logarithmic derivative and runs from infinity to zero, giving one simple root for every m. The nonvanishing factors in these two ratio equations preserve simplicity. The degree gives the nonreal counts and the real-rooted cases exactly m=1,2. The latter ratio equation gives y_m>3^m−1 and 0<log[(y_m+1)/3^m]≤2m/[3(y_m−1)]→0. The bounded branch has (3x_m−1)/(1−x_m)=(1+x_m)^(1/m)→1 uniformly on its interval, forcing x_m→1/2. Replay: python3 /workspace/reproduce_reviews.py 2 independently enumerated the histogram and checked exact signs at −1 and −1/2 through m=7; this finite evidence does not certify the unrestricted root statements.

value.rationale: A subdivided star is a natural minimal extension of a path and a useful family outside the claw-free real-rootedness hypotheses. It exhibits an exact boundary of real-rootedness and, at growing degree, a bounded count of simple real roots with parity-dependent branch structure. Quantifying the escape rate 3^m and the bounded limit makes the conclusion useful beyond a few small nonreal examples. The all-length tree problem is not claimed.
